Explicit Go121 compatibility profile uses 301. BOTH Go1.26.5 and Go1.27.1 modern sources use 307. Go126 retains its decoded/escaped redirect construction, while Go127 uses urlFromEscaped to preserve encoded separators and avoid double escaping.
Redirect Location non-ASCII escaping, HTML link escaping, existing Content-Type behavior, GET/HEAD content-type and GET-only short body including the second newline.

Incoming request initializes one byte-preserving SourceUrl with decoded Path and RawPath hint. Mux/callback mutations use that same owner. Malformed path escapes return 400 before callbacks; CONNECT authority-form has empty URL.Path. Native parser/authority profiles remain partial.

Native informational response path: source writer -> bounded per-request InformationalSender -> existing H1 driver/encoder/flush acknowledgement or existing H2 stream SendResponse::send_informational. Intermediate headers leave the final response and handler header map uncommitted and uncleared.

HTTP/1 101 remains a final upgrade response; bundled Go HTTP/2 treats its 1xx class separately. HTTP/1 explicit 100 or final headers disable deferred automatic Continue. HTTP/2 body-read Continue remains its separate source state, including source Expect removal and multi-value token rules.

Server-level OPTIONS * bypasses mux dispatch, emits zero Content-Length, drains up to the source 4KB bound and closes an oversized HTTP/1 connection. Unknown HTTP/1 expectations produce the source empty 417 with Connection close before user handlers.

Full ordered 512-byte Go sniff table includes HTML/XML/PDF/PostScript/BOM/images/audio/video/MP4/fonts/archives/WASM/text. Detection uses the first emitted buffered chunk, not the first small handler write.

ResponseWriter now owns source 2048-byte H1 and 4096-byte H2 buffering, direct large writes, header snapshots and no-body/HEAD/header-presence/Content-Encoding/Transfer-Encoding decisions. H1 signed length parsing and H2 deferred unsigned-63-bit parsing retain their distinct count/error and empty-write behavior.

Attempted int64 write count wraps and includes rejected length overruns; failed transport writes retain the original error chain through one shared sticky failure. Header transport failures are ignored as in source WriteHeader, while the native connection retains its failure.

Source clock and default HTTP diagnostic capabilities are statically supplied by UtilityRuntimeProviders. Date is generated only when its header key is absent, with native automatic dates disabled; Go status-line strings and unknown-code fallback are supplied to the existing reason-phrase extension.

Hyper H2 stream/upgrade futures now use a weak executor and the existing per-connection UtilityTaskScope. Normal/error connection exits cancel and join protocol children; emergency scope Drop aborts owned children. No discarded TokioExecutor JoinHandles or competing lifecycle manager.

Trailer declarations now follow source comma/ASCII-space splitting, canonicalization and the exact httpguts forbidden-name table. H1 retains duplicate declarations and prefixed fields; H2 de-duplicates and promotes prefixed fields with unordered canonical-key collision choices.

Actual response trailer I/O: ResponseWriter publishes one source-encoded H1 field block before yielding its trailers frame. The pinned native connection consumes it only for this response's chunked body, independent of client TE or prior Trailer declarations. Source Header.Write sorting, key spelling, CR/LF replacement and trimming are authored. H2 emits actual trailers frames through the existing h2 body sender, including key-presence with empty values.

Bounded response messages now carry end-of-stream decisions. HTTP/2 HEAD and completed empty responses can end on HEADERS, final data can carry END_STREAM, and present trailers end on their HEADERS frame. This is authored source control flow, not a native frame/parity observation.

Source HTTP/2 Connection first-value exactly close removes that field and signals its connection-owned graceful-close token. The existing Hyper connection driver owns shutdown/GOAWAY and independent stream draining; no new server or task manager.

Plain and TLS accept loops share one per-listener AcceptBackoff, 5ms doubling to 1s, reset on success, via static CGP SourceHttpDelay. Error handling checks shutdown before retry and retains permanent native errors. The source syscall-wrapped Unix/Windows Errno policy is distinct from the direct-Errno exception and Winsock lookalikes; native error-origin and display profiles remain open.

Original transport RequestBody remains one owner for Incoming, pending data, trailers, remaining/closed/EOF/early-close state and H2 close/read wakeup. Current Request.Body and expectation-wrapper flags are now distinct retained owners described below.

HTTP/1 pre-response discard now retains the 256KB threshold and separate limit+1 read rule. H1 Close uses its distinct strict-greater-than size rule, fixed copy bound, early-close flag and request-closing/chunked branch. OPTIONS reads at most its remaining 4KB limit plus one source byte per call. Body Close is async and the existing FourZeroFour caller awaits it after the successful-read/error-response path.

Source H1 framing decisions now include inferred lengths, HEAD/no-body suppression, identity versus chunked transfer, conflicting Transfer-Encoding/Content-Length handling, HTTP/1.0 keep-alive and close rules, Continue-reader EOF, source full-duplex opt-in, Date/sniff/header-key presence and protocol-switch Connection preservation. The source handler fields and extraHeader fields remain separate output stages; the latter use Date/length/type/connection/transfer order.

SourceResponse carries immutable H1 fields/framing into the existing native role/connection encoder. Normal and informational source fields use Go Header.Write byte normalization, original key spelling and sorted map order. Source chunks use lowercase hex. Source Content-Length mode does not add native truncation, a competing attempted-byte counter, or an early body-end decision; the source writer retains wrapping/rejected-write accounting.

SourceResponseEnd is published once by the existing request phase after handler return and body cleanup, with declared-length/attempted-count, write-failure, close-after-reply and early-body-close decisions. The existing H1 driver waits before reuse, including HEAD/no-body replies, and preserves queued I/O. Emergency request-phase Drop publishes close. No new actor, executor, registry or lifecycle manager.

Connection disposal now cancels its request children through the existing connection phase. Normal H1 response-body disposal no longer cancels a still-running no-body handler; H2 keeps independent stream/body disposal cancellation. Production parent/source-profile and native schedule reconciliation remain open.

Source H1 heads now bypass the native response-metadata keep-alive heuristic, including separately encoded HTTP/1.0 extra fields. Explicit native shutdown is retained and cannot be re-enabled by a source head. Source close-delimited output likewise defers physical close to handler/body-cleanup completion rather than ending that phase at byte EOF.

Headers now retains raw byte names, nil-map identity and shared map descriptors; HeaderValues retains nil versus non-nil empty, an independent length/capacity/offset view and one shared backing owner. Map clone, shallow copy and source deep copy are distinct operations. Indexed writes and in-capacity append retain aliases; growth allocates separate backing. Value iteration reads shared slots rather than an eager value snapshot.

H1 response snapshots use Header.Clone's combined backing and clipped per-key capacities, nil-value preservation and source-int total-count behavior. Bundled H2 uses its separate per-key clone and nil-to-non-nil-empty rule. Informational filtering uses a new map without clearing the handler map. Native H1 header serialization still sorts raw keys independently of source map iteration.

Header append capacity has explicit Go1.26 word32/word64 and heap-address parameters, signed nextslicecap arithmetic, pointer-containing string size-class/header rounding and source-word page-rounding overflow. The current constructor explicitly selects Go126/64/48; actual source tool/ABI/configuration binding remains M0027, without Rust-host capacity inference.

Source LogRequest now retains the redacted header map as SourceLogValue::HttpHeaders until the existing CGP logger serializes. Non-sensitive value arrays remain shared, sensitive values are independent REDACTED slices, and WithField replaces the typed field normally. Header JSON retains nil/null versus empty arrays/maps, raw-byte key sort, duplicate keys after UTF8 replacement, per-invalid-byte escaped UFFFD versus literal valid UFFFD, HTML and JS-separator escaping through the already enabled serde_json RawValue capability.

Requests initialize declared trailer maps with nil values and source H1/H2 forbidden/empty-element rules, retain non-chunked H1 Trailer headers, remove selected trailer declarations from the request header map and merge actual trailers into the same map owner. H2 request Cookie lines join with semicolon-space. Request, response, trailer, gateway and logging consumers use the same typed header data.

HttpRequest and ResponseWriter share RequestFields for live method bytes, ContentLength and current Body. Mux, gateway method override, APIServer GET dispatch and HTTP response framing read that shared owner; pre-handler wantsClose/wants10 snapshots remain intentional.

SourceBody retains NoBody, native, H1 expectContinueReader, H2 reader, io.NopCloser(bytes.Reader), nil or one custom SourceReadCloser receiver. Cloning retains the interface receiver/cursor; replacing Request.Body does not mutate the retained original body or close the replacement during server cleanup.

H1 framing inspects current Body type/closed/remaining/expect-EOF state, but io.CopyN discard and finishRequest Close use the original response.reqBody. The final early-close type assertion applies only to the current native H1 Body, excluding expectation wrappers and custom readers.

SourceBodyRead retains data and an optional exact EOF/failure category together. Native known-length H1 reads pair their last data with EOF while holding the body lock; expectation EOF is set from that read result. H2 keeps its subsequent-read EOF behavior. Empty successful reads are not EOF.

H1 automatic Continue Read and final/explicit-100 disable share the same lock; its available flag clears after flush. Replacing Body bypasses the old wrapper; a retained old wrapper still owns its closed/EOF state. H2 clears needsContinue before sending and before checking its pipe.

ReadAll retains its initial Reader, starts at 512 logical source bytes, applies source byte-slice nextslicecap/noscan size-class growth and consumes returned bytes before an error. Its low-level result retains partial bytes on failure. Form parsing wraps the retained Reader with a 10MiB+1 limit, preserving ReadAll error precedence before size rejection.

SourceJsonDecoder is shared by webhook and gateway consumers: retain the Reader, compact only on refill, grow logical capacity by 2*cap+512, scan data before its paired read error, and discard that local error if a value completes. Sticky framing/read failures and successful semantic decoding remain separate.

H1 byte suppression and final length/reuse checks read the current Method; a previously selected chunked response still emits its final chunk after Method becomes HEAD. Source Empty headers use a native unframed body kept alive through the source phase, allowing subsequent Method reassignment without native length-zero truncation.

SourceByteString and SourceLogValue::Bytes preserve original method/body bytes until Go JSON escaping, including per-invalid-byte escapes. FourZeroFour captures the successful-path deferred Body receiver before logging/writing; the existing CGP body-I/O capability closes that retained receiver.

RequestFields now owns optional SourceUrl, Host and RequestURI bytes in addition to method/ContentLength/Body. HttpRequest no longer stores separate path/host/query or precomputed JSON snapshots; its path and escaped-path accessors read the current URL owner.

SourceUrl Clone retains pointer identity; fields() copies the URL value and new(fields) creates a different URL pointer while retaining immutable strings and Userinfo. URL replacement and in-place field mutation are distinct. Nil URL logs serialize null; source URL dereferences retain a panic boundary.

SourceUrlFields retains arbitrary bytes in Scheme/Opaque/Host/Path/Fragment/RawQuery/RawPath/RawFragment plus User/ForceQuery/OmitHost. URL JSON follows the common Go1.26.5/Go1.27.1 field declaration order and existing SourceByteString escaping. Non-nil immutable Userinfo serializes its empty exported-field shape rather than username/password data.

SourceLogValue::Url and LogEntry::with_url retain the selected URL pointer through field-map copies. HTTPS LogRequest and webhook error logging serialize later mutations of that same object; Request.URL replacement does not retarget saved entries. Host and RequestURI use original-byte string log fields.

Modern and legacy muxes read current URL.Path/RawPath/Host/RawQuery and byte Host/RequestURI values. EscapedPath validates the current RawPath hint against current decoded Path. Host comparisons and port stripping retain bytes instead of creating lossy text projections; routing/profile/parser gaps remain explicit.

HTTPS default root matching and APIServer namespace/resource extraction consume current URL path bytes. CRDHandler namespace and delegate lookup keys now retain Bytes, including malformed/non-UTF8 path values. General Go error Display and typed resource/model boundaries remain separate gaps.

Gateway dispatch captures current URL.Path before its ParseForm/body reader call, as in source. Form query parsing reads current URL.RawQuery after the body read and permits nil URL. Gateway component/parameter/form text representations, form caches/partial states and parameter-limit binding remain explicit unfinished work.

SourceValues reuses the existing shared byte-key map/string-slice backing with exact case-sensitive append, nil versus empty maps/slices, indexed aliases, source allocation capacity and existing JSON byte-string serialization. GatewayCall.form now retains that map rather than a lossy BTreeMap<String,Vec<String>>.

RequestFields owns nil-initialized Form and PostForm; getters/assignment retain map identities. The fixed gateway fallback preserves ParseForm cache order: parse PostForm even when Form is already set, allocate an empty PostForm after failed/absent body parsing, copy body values first, merge current URL query second, and skip already initialized caches on later calls.

URL query parsing returns a non-nil map and optional error together. It continues past bad names/values, preserves all valid pairs, appends duplicate values in input order, keeps the first escape error, and lets each later semicolon error overwrite the prior error as in the source. QueryUnescape retains arbitrary bytes and plus-to-space behavior; typed invalid escapes retain the original at-most-three-byte segment.

The fixed gateway form path retains nil-Body missing-form error, ReadAll bytes/error handling, 10MiB+1 body bound and POST-too-large result. It assigns partial PostForm values on query errors, still populates Form from the current optional URL after body errors, and preserves the body error over the later query error. Cached errors are not replayed once the source maps are initialized.

SourceQueryProfile explicitly supplies source allocation/word size and selected urlmaxqueryparams bytes. Both selected Go sources default to at most 10000 ampersand-counted parameters; valid custom values use zero=unlimited or params<custom, invalid/source-int-overflow values fall back to default, negative values retain their source comparison, and a differing default/custom decision increments the shared nondefault counter. The source second setting read before Atoi is retained.

UtilityRuntimeProviders statically delegates SourceQuerySettingsGetter through UseField(source_query_settings); UtilityRuntimeOwner constructs one explicit Go126/64 default data profile. No Rust-host fallback, environment probe, automatic GODEBUG binding, native metric publication or completed source-profile credit is inferred.

Gateway dispatch splits the captured URL.Path into Bytes without UTF8-lossy conversion. Pattern literals, verbs, wildcard/multi/concat stacks, capture names and values retain bytes through the actual raw callback; duplicate capture keys overwrite in source variable order in a HashMap<Bytes,Bytes>.

GatewayPattern.new retains the supplied HeaderValues []string slice backing and its view length/capacity. Literal operations and source string rendering read the live pool. NewPattern copies variable name values when processing capture operations, so later pool edits do not rename captures. Registered pattern copies retain that same literal backing.

Byte suffix splitting preserves exact colon/verb bytes, including a verb containing a colon, empty-prefix 404 handling on same-method routes and the separate other-method fallback path. GatewayPattern.string_bytes is the canonical Pattern.String operation; fmt::Display is only a lossy text compatibility view.

SourceUppercaseMapper is statically delegated through UtilityRuntimeProviders and reads the SourceUnicodeProfile getter. Header override bytes captured before ParseForm are mapped afterward through the same runtime context. Go single-rune uppercase and per-invalid-byte UTF8 replacement replace the prior Rust expanding/lossy conversion.

The Rust reader projects only numeric CaseRanges uppercase deltas into disposable OnceLock lookup caches, then uses source binary-range lookup and UpperLower even-offset conversion. No production Go body is parsed/evaluated and no Rust source is generated from Go text.

The default runtime context explicitly selects Go1265. Both source Unicode profiles are authored, but actual application/compiler/profile binding, source string/builder identity/capacity/allocation/panic behavior and native integration remain unverified required work.

GatewayPattern.new now accepts i64 version/opcode operands with an explicit Go32/Go64 PatternWordProfile. Ingress values and stack/tail arithmetic use source-word normalization/wrapping. All constructor rejection branches carry their exact selected numeric value/message through the existing CGP runtime.

PatternConstruction retains a zero GatewayPattern plus an optional shared-identity invalid-pattern error on rejection, and the real pattern plus nil error on success. into_result is an explicit Rust projection. InvalidPatternError copies retain one private static identity token; direct equality helper is distinct from wrapped-error traversal.

Constructor diagnostics distinguish unsupported version, odd opcode count, duplicate pushM, literal/concat/capture indices, stack underflow and invalid opcode with the source messages, including source misleading negative-literal wording for positive out-of-bounds indices.

SourcePatternLogger models the default Error/Fatal stderr profile plus explicit discard/JSON choices. It checks discard before formatting user Error values, uses source severity prefixes/local standard-log date-time or sorted JSON message/severity fields, appends only a missing newline and ignores the single Write result. General formatter/caller/native writer/global configuration profiles remain open.

MustPattern is consumed by SourceGatewayPatternConstructor.require_source_gateway_pattern: nil error returns the given pattern; nonnil error emits the fatal initialization message and invokes the existing CGP SourceProcessExit(1). An unexpectedly returning exit provider panics instead of reporting success. No fatal path was executed.

GatewayContext new_pattern/must_pattern/handle_compiled provide a connected compiled-registration path through RuntimeProviders and the existing route table. Actual generated SDK/allocator initializer and command adoption remains M0025/M0027, without registration-only acceptance credit.

GatewayPattern retains its explicit PatternWordProfile through successful/rejected construction, zero(profile), cloning and registered routes. max_int is source i32::MAX/i64::MAX, independent of the Rust host.

Source strings.Join slash helper preserves empty/single-element fast paths, including immutable single-string reuse, the source strict separator >= maxInt/(count-1) guard and ordered element remaining-length checks.

Source concat helper skips empty parts, reuses a sole nonempty immutable string and checks the selected source integer bound before concatenating. Matcher verb fallback and the no-verb Pattern.String slash prefix consume it.

Pattern.String capture braces and nonempty-verb rendering follow their two fixed byte-only Sprintf forms, with per-append source-int overflow classification kept distinct from runtime concatenation. This is not a general Go formatter or a complete printer-pool/heap/allocator profile.

SourcePatternStringCompletion routes Join overflow to a string panic, fixed-format overflow to a typed recoverable runtime-error projection, and concat overflow to stderr fatal prefix plus SourceProcessExit(2). A returning exit provider aborts; runtime.throw is not downgraded to recoverable panic or pattern-logger output.

GatewayDispatcher passes its runtime capability for both same-method and other-method matching. Canonical Pattern.string_bytes consumes the same provider; try_string_bytes returns an explicit Rust result and Display returns fmt::Error on a length failure rather than claiming source effect equivalence.

Matcher borrows the input components on equal verbs and rejects a nonempty mismatching pattern verb before copying. It copies only when source verb fallback must change the last component; empty fallback creates one component.

PatternSourceProfile derives source integer width from its retained shared HeaderAllocationProfile. Explicit Go32/Go64 conversions select Go1.26 word/heap defaults; callers can supply another explicit Go1.26 allocation profile. Zero/error/registered copies retain the same profile; actual process target binding remains M0027.

Join uses fresh Builder/MakeNoZero allocation limits and rounded capacity after its existing integer-length checks. A source makeslice failure is distinct from Join string overflow, native address-space limits and native allocation failure.

Fixed pattern Sprintf forms track logical source byte capacity, allocate replacement storage at source growslice points and copy the completed []byte into separate string storage before releasing the fresh scratch buffer. Empty/single-byte string conversion paths use empty/static immutable storage.

String allocation uses fallible native reservation. Source makeslice/growslice projections remain recoverable; source heap/native OOM uses fatal out-of-memory prefix plus the existing process-exit 2 capability. Native address-space failure remains a separately named hosting limitation.

Pattern opcode operands, stacksize, tailLen and match position retain signed source int values. PushM uses wrapped source pos+tail/end-tail in source order; concat/capture use source subtraction before checked indexing or slicing.

Components, stacks, captured strings and copied variable-name storage reuse HeaderValues length/capacity/backing. Stack truncation reslices rather than dropping backing slots. Join reads slice values directly and preserves zero/single-element fast paths.

PatternBoundsError carries source x/y/signed/code with source negative and unsigned formatting families. Pattern index/slice helpers check source upper-capacity before lower-bound order and retain runtime.boundsError origin through the existing SourceErrorOrigin template.

Logical make([]string,len,cap) retains len-versus-capacity error precedence and selected source element/heap limits before native layout conversion. Native backing allocation/runtime panic/failure ordering remains explicit unfinished work.

PatternSentinelError gives ErrNotMatch and ErrInvalidPattern one errors.errorString source class and separate private singleton identities. Direct identity helpers remain distinct from wrapped error traversal; aliases share the same underlying Rust class.

Canonical match_source returns PatternMatchResult through the static CGP provider. Dispatcher matches is an explicit Option projection; try_matches/try_string_bytes preserve typed operation-failure results for Rust callers without pretending those projections execute source panic/throw effects.

ServeMux verb suffix concatenation now completes through the same source profile/provider. The same-method empty-prefix 404 returns before component make/copy; the other-method case still makes the source untrimmed copy. Per-route component copies have source logical length/capacity.

HeaderAllocationProfile provides shared make_slice_layout/grow_slice_layout results with source element size, pointer scanning/class rounding, source heap/word bounds and selected malloc byte request. Existing string/byte growth calculations reuse that arithmetic.

HeaderValues.try_make/try_append_values/try_append_slice use fallible native array reservation, preserve source logical capacity/backing and distinguish makeslice/growslice, native address-space and native OOM outcomes. Alias append uses one lock with memmove direction; single-value append avoids a temporary Vec.

PatternOperationBuilder grows pointer-free op pairs at two source words per element and records source capacity independently of native Vec capacity. Returned PatternOperations shares immutable backing across route/Pattern clones, preserving nil typed ops without deep copies.

Canonical construction uses owned immutable Bytes for verb data and completes try_new outcomes through existing static CGP. Variable-name, stack, capture and component-copy storage consumes the fallible HeaderValues path; failures are not converted to invalid-pattern errors or non-matches.

PatternInputDomainError identifies Rust bridge lengths/address spans outside the selected Go word domain. Constructor/matcher/renderer/verb splitting check relevant opcode, pool, component and string lengths without attributing rejected foreign inputs to Go panic/error credit.

StringBacking distinguishes Nil, Empty and allocated Slots. Zero-capacity non-nil string slices retain JSON/alias/nil semantics without allocating an Arc/RwLock backing object; allocated reslices still retain their backing.

Native public HeaderValues make/append/materialization/parsing use the existing fallible slice/storage operations and a statically selected SourceCollectionFailureRaiser. HTTP1 clone total/make and HTTP2 per-value copies consume the same policy, with owned key headers reused.

SourceRuntimeAllocationError carries runtime.errorString origin and allocation text; SourceNilMapAssignment carries runtime.plainError origin and nil-map text. Existing SourceErrorOrigin derives declarations, without claiming full Go interface/type equivalence.

Recoverable collection and selected pattern bounds/Join/allocation failures use resume_unwind with the original typed payload, avoiding Rust's eager hook before the owning recovery policy. No global panic hook, replacement task owner or panic/abort-profile assurance is introduced.

Header Add and exact append/copy read the old slice, complete RHS append, then assign the map. A failed append does not insert a new nil-valued key; nil-map assignment occurs after RHS allocation. SourceValues single add and slice copy avoid temporary Vec staging.

NativeSourceCollectionProviders and existing UtilityRuntimeProviders statically bind the same collection failure provider plus SourceProcessExit. Recoverable failures unwind; OOM emits its fatal prefix and exits 2; an unexpectedly returning exit aborts. No failure or native path ran.

Headers.try_insert reserves native HashMap capacity before inserting a new key; replacing an existing key skips table reservation. Public insertion completes failures through the existing collection effect and preserves nil-map behavior.

Header key/field snapshots use bounded fallible native reservations; public iteration, sorting and shallow/HTTP1/HTTP2 clones consume their try_* paths. Unique map keys use sort_unstable_by for identical byte ordering without merge scratch allocation.

HeaderName.try_new and try_canonical_header_key/try_set_header expose fallible name/value materialization. Setter and clone paths reuse owned key headers without another insertion copy; public helpers use the existing static failure policy.

HeaderValues/Headers.try_json_bytes and the shared byte-string encoder reserve native byte capacity fallibly while retaining existing nil/null/empty, sorted-key, HTML/control/UTF8 replacement/U2028/U2029 escaping behavior. Serializer/RawValue/control allocation remains explicit unfinished work.

runtime.Must preserves nil and quietly unwinds a SourceErrorPanic retaining the original BoxError; source Error access does not introduce an Unwrap layer. SourceRecoveredPanic can retain/resume the original catch payload and expose selected runtime-error and source-type views.

Canonical SourceRuntimeErrorString, SourceNilMapAssignment and SourceBoundsError/Code implement the no-op RuntimeError marker and derive source origin/log types. Existing SourceRuntimeAllocationError and PatternBoundsError/Code names are aliases of shared types; no duplicate bounds formatter.

Selected source allocation/nil-map/pattern-bounds/header-set/full-reslice/nil-body/invalid-WriteHeader paths quietly unwind typed runtime errors or source strings. Header full slices check maximum/capacity, high/maximum then low/high; native unsigned index views remain an explicit bridge profile.
Private ErrAbortHandler token preserves direct sentinel equality. HTTP recovery suppresses reporting for that direct value, while wrapped sentinel errors retain ordinary reporting.

Existing HTTP request tasks catch only the authored handler/expectation/OPTIONS phase, apply H1 report-before-cancel/Continue-disable/original-body cleanup and H2 cancel/unfinished-writer failure-before-report branches, then complete the existing response phase. Finish/cleanup panic coverage, hijack/multipart/pending-read and native reset/close schedules remain open.

SourceHttpPanicReporter is selected by the existing derive-deftly UtilityRuntimeProviders and uses the existing diagnostic and collection-failure effects. It emits protocol-specific panic prefixes and a bounded native recovery stack; source Go traceback/caller parity is not claimed. Native plaintext/TLS accept phases pass accepted peer text without new state owners.

finish_source_request retains the existing writer/original-body/early-close operation order. H2 handler success exits its catch before cancellation and finishing, retaining its distinct didPanic/handlerDone boundary. Existing response-phase ownership closes failed H1 work.

SourceRuntimeErrorEnvelope, with_runtime_error and SourceRuntimeError.into_source_error retain the original error, RuntimeError method and declared source type across a BoxError boundary. The envelope delegates its original source chain rather than creating a source Unwrap edge.

One runtime_error_views! declaration covers canonical runtime.errorString/plainError/boundsError owned, borrowed and type views. Must recognizes those direct BoxError classes and typed envelopes without stringification, reboxing canonical objects or classifying a wrapper's child as the wrapper's RuntimeError interface.

SourceRecoveredPanic exposes original errors and runtime/type views for native boxed payloads. Existing errors.first_error_view traverses the runtime envelope's original value and its real source chain, preserving the existing ordered multiple-cause traversal. Full custom Is/As/composed interface behavior remains required.

UtilityRuntimeProviders statically selects SourceRuntimePanicReporter -> ReportNativeSourceRuntimePanic and SourceUtilityPanicHandler -> ExitAfterSourceUtilityPanic alongside existing SourceProcessExit. Runtime context and lifecycle owners retain the same resources.

SpawnOwnedUtilityTask wraps existing child futures in source_utility_task. An unhandled poll panic is delivered as its original SourceRecoveredPanic to the selected terminal policy; ordinary Result errors retain existing observer/join/caller handling. The context clone holds a Weak task-scope reference, not its supervisor.

The native parent reporter converts selected Error/string values before stack capture, indents embedded panic newlines, and handles a panic during value printing through a fatal-error branch without recursively formatting that second value. Source panic chains, full types/printing and runtime trace modes remain required.

ExitAfterSourceUtilityPanic retains a reporting failure until termination, emits the native panic-during-panic fallback if reporting unwinds, and calls the existing process-exit effect with status2, then aborts if it returns. It does not suppress ErrAbortHandler or cancel/join unrelated children before its terminal decision. Native/Go exit, hook, crash and concurrency profiles are unverified and incomplete.

New spawn_utility_task_or_return returns its guarded live future if the parent is closed/released. retain_connection_drain uses that CGP boundary; caller-side cancellation and inline join retain the original connection/request resources on rejection.

HTTP and parent panic reporters share native_recovery_stack and one bounded buffer implementation. This is a native Rust recovery-frame adapter, not source Go traceback evidence; the HTTP suppression and diagnostic path remain separate from root fatal output.

Root SourceCrashState owns ReallyCrash (default true) and the default one-element LogPanic callback slice. Existing derive-deftly UtilityRuntimeProviders selects its getter, crash handler and diagnostic reporter; workers share this state through the same runtime context.

SourcePanicHandlers supports nil/non-nil-empty/fixed backing slots, index/full-reslice operations and source-profile make/append growth. A range captures the header and length, then copies each current function slot separately without holding locks over user callbacks. Later-slot writes are visible; reassigned/grown headers do not redirect the captured range.

Nil handlers quietly raise the canonical runtime nil-memory error; callback failures stop later handlers and preserve the new payload.

This scoped control path does not stringify or fabricate the payload. General retained/cross-goroutine Go panic-value semantics remain required.

The native reporter retains Observed a panic, panic/stacktrace and string-versus-panicGoValue field branches, with Rust Debug/recovery-stack output explicitly partial. True/rethrown failures reach the existing parent panic guard.

Recoverable collection and selected pattern bounds/Join/allocation failures use resume_unwind with the original typed payload, avoiding Rust's eager hook before the owning recovery policy. No global panic hook, replacement task owner or panic/abort-profile assurance is introduced.

authored_operations: SourcePrintfPlan scans arbitrary format bytes into retained literal ranges and directive spans, flags, width/precision specifications, decoded rune verbs and Value/Percent/BadIndex/MissingArgument/NoVerb outcomes. Invalid UTF8 consumes one byte and uses RuneError; a terminal dot is a verb while an empty precision before another byte is zero.

parse_number preserves the pinned parsenum pre-digit 1e6 overflow check and its end-of-input consumption, including the accepted final digit above that bound. Bracket parsing consumes through a closing bracket or only the opening byte if absent, distinguishes syntactic presence from an out-of-range argument and retains reordered on malformed indexes.

Source argument consumption preserves initial/width/precision/final indexes, present invalid star operands, missing-star cursor retention, percent priority over bad-index/missing-operand outcomes, no-verb termination and suppression of trailing extra arguments after any explicit index.

SourcePrintfDirective.resolve_counts reads width then precision integer kinds once, rejects star magnitudes outside plus/minus 1e6, makes negative widths positive and sets minus/clears zero, and rejects negative precision. Ordered BadWidth/BadPrecision data precedes the verb result. Literal numbers retain the distinct parsenum range.

Value v/w directives move sharp/plus into sharpV/plusV state. Every in-range w occurrence is recorded before error-type validation, retaining repeated explicit positions and invalid/nil error operands for the existing canonical factory.

SourceFormat.scanned derives wrapping/reordered metadata directly from original format bytes and optional error operands. Existing Errorf consumes the resulting state through its unchanged canonical factory; rendered output is still supplied by the caller. The indexed compatibility bridge, source class selection and multiple/single unwrap distinction remain in place.

Nanosecond masking, packed wall seconds, monotonic set/strip, zero detection, instant equality/comparison and retained location copies are authored from pinned Go source. Time source fields are exposed only through the existing typed formatter; native Arc pointers/fields are not claimed as Go header/GC/ABI evidence.

Unix/millisecond/microsecond/nanosecond conversion and constructor normalization preserve signed division/remainder, negative nanoseconds and explicit wrapping int64 arithmetic. Source Add retains or degrades packed monotonic data, applies the exact addSec saturation endpoints and detects monotonic overflow; Sub uses source replay equality and minimum/maximum duration saturation.

Source location setters strip monotonic data and canonicalize only the actual UTC singleton; In(nil) raises the exact source string panic. UTC and FixedZone named/unnamed identity and the specific -12h..+14h unnamed fixed cache are authored. Rule/local lookup/name/current-Local callbacks retain concrete native data supplied by the existing CGP owner. Dynamic loader/TZ/local/global/native effect bindings remain open.

Slog TimeValue handles zero separately, performs the wrapped UnixNano/instant-equality fit test, stores compact nanoseconds plus the retained location when representable, and otherwise stores a full Round(0)-normalized Time. Time/Any reconstruction, String/Equal and source reference copies are connected. The private slog.timeTime wrapper has its own underlying type fields and does not inherit Time methods.

Source calendar conversion retains the unsigned absolute epoch, Mul32 high/low halves, March-based century/year/day/month arithmetic and source clock decomposition. Time.String preserves fraction trimming, raw zone names/empty-name numeric fallback, minute truncation and signed monotonic suffix including minimum int64 magnitude. Native Go32/year/offset/layout/calendar profiles remain required.

Time.GoString emits source Date/month/location syntax, canonical UTC and supplied current-Local identity. Its time.quote implementation hex-escapes every original non-ASCII/control byte and leaves DEL literal, rather than substituting strconv.Quote. Full Local reassignment/native identity/initialization and general time formatting APIs remain required.

Time MarshalJSON authors quoted strict RFC3339Nano output, source year-width and timezone-hour validation, source minute-offset behavior, final quote before returned-error discard and the exact inner Time.MarshalJSON errors. Its Encoder.Encode projection appends LF and creates the real declared time-specific json.MarshalerError wrapper on a source returned error.

SourceTimeMarshalerError preserves the original retained error, correct *json.MarshalerError source identity, Error prefix and actual single Unwrap method. Direct type/message/query/operand/base formatting bindings are registered alongside existing concrete source declarations. Full mutable exported fields, arbitrary receiver state, native reflect.Type/rtype/base field binding and typed nils remain explicit gaps.

Host declaration failures raised during native/source formatting now bypass Go fmt panic recovery and are returned at the typed klog boundary with their original operation. Nil receiver and ordinary source panic handling is unchanged. Native binding failures do not become fabricated source panic diagnostics or false nil-receiver success.

SourcePrintfInterfaces and SourceErrorOrigin derive the real Time Stringer/GoStringer/JSON and json.MarshalerError Error/Unwrap method sets. Existing typed retained arguments, source error carriers, callback slices and CGP runtime/crash/Unicode/collection/logger/task owners remain canonical; no general Go object interpreter, provider/type registry, orchestrator integration or competing manager is introduced.

Existing native crash string fields remain connected through that dispatcher. Native time effects/full type and remaining logger/context/sink adoption are still required.
